message.content:
Explore /home/nick/work/andesim (a C++/C project: QEMU TCG plugin + a C++ driver + a runtime + shell test harnesses). I need to know everything relevant to adding/running CODE COVERAGE for recently-modified functions.

Search "very thorough" and report:

1. Build system: what builds what. Read scripts/build_all.sh, setup.sh, config.env.example, and any Makefiles (qemu_plugin/Makefile, runtime/Makefile, tests/fixtures/Makefile, src/ Makefile or CMakeLists). Report exact compiler invocations, CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS variables, and whether flags can be overridden from the environment (e.g. CFLAGS ?= or += patterns). Quote the relevant lines.

2. What source is HOST code (compiled for x86-64 host, i.e. coverage-able with gcc --coverage / llvm-cov) vs TARGET RISC-V code (fixtures, runtime -- not coverage-able the same way). Specifically: where does the C++ `andesim` driver live (src/? which files), and how does it self-build (the CLAUDE.md says "self-builds on first use") -- find the exact code/script that compiles it and the flags used.

3. Any EXISTING coverage support: grep the whole repo for gcov, lcov, gcovr, --coverage, -fprofile, llvm-cov, kcov, COVERAGE, .gcda, .gcno, codecov. Report every hit with file:line.

4. Test entry points: scripts/test_all.sh (what phases: unit/contract/e2e), scripts/run_e2e.sh, tests/andes_sim/*.sh, tests/plugin/*.sh. Report roughly how many tests each phase has and how long they seem to take (any timeouts in the scripts).

5. Toolchain available: check which compilers exist on this host (gcc, clang versions), and whether gcov/lcov/gcovr/llvm-cov are installed (run `which` / `--version` for each).

6. Git: run `git -C /home/nick/work/andesim log --oneline -20` and `git diff --stat main...HEAD` (branch is llamacpp) and `git diff --stat HEAD~5..HEAD` to identify which files have been modified recently. Report the list of modified HOST source files specifically.

Report file paths and quoted snippets. Do NOT modify anything.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Build the user-facing andesim runtime library into build/runtime/:
2	#
3	#   libandesim_runtime.a   trap.o handler.o htif_client.o vplat_syscalls.o
4	#   crt0.o                   startfile; kept OUTSIDE the archive because
5	#                            nothing references _start, so the linker
6	#                            would never extract it from a .a (same
7	#                            reason toolchains ship crt0.o next to libc.a)
8	#   andesim.ld             linker script (load base 0x00100000)
9	#   include/andesim/ROI.h  ROI markers (HINT NOPs; same dir rides -B)
10	#
11	# Users link with:
12	#   gcc ... -B <repo>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs hello.c
13	# or, without the gcc driver:
14	#   gcc ... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T andesim.ld crt0.o hello.c \
15	#       -L <repo>/build/runtime \
16	#       -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
17	#
18	# Toolchain location comes from config.env (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN), same as
19	# tests/fixtures/Makefile.
20	
21	# ARCH selects the target width: rv64 (default) or rv32. Each arch has its own
22	# toolchain (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN / HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32), triple, -march/-mabi, and
23	# output dir. rv64 stays at build/runtime (back-compat with `-B build/runtime`);
24	# rv32 lands at build/runtime/rv32 (`-B build/runtime/rv32`).

30	  ARCHFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d
31	  OUT       ?= ../build/runtime

34	  TRIPLE    := riscv32-unknown-elf
35	  ARCHFLAGS := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d
36	  OUT       ?= ../build/runtime/rv32

39	endif
40	
41	ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)

46	AR := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-ar

49	# attributes), so one build serves both -march variants of the arch.

64

12	rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
13	CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
14	CXX       = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-g++

20	# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
21	RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
22	LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
23	# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
24	HELPERS_DIR := runtime
25	
26	CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
27	LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static
28	
29	# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
30	RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
31	               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
32	               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
33	               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
34	
35	# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
36	# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
37	# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)

39	                  break_verify_diverge
40	
41	# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
42	# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
43	# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
44	# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
45	# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
46	# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
47	# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
48	# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
49	# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
50	# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
51	RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
52	                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
53	RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill \
54	                    rt_c_hvm_data
55	RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file vplat_gettimeofday \
56	                       vplat_window
57	# C++ vplat smoke fixture: static ctors/dtors + libstdc++ containers
58	# through the same two-flag link, with g++ instead of gcc.
59	RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_cpp
60	
61	RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
62	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
63	# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
64	RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
65	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/htif_client.c $(RUNTIME_DIR)/htif_client.h \
66	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
67	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
68	VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
69	VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
70	                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
71	                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
72	VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
73	# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
74	# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
75	# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
76	VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
77	
78	# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
79	# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
80	# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
81	# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin

83	TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
84	CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
85	LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
86	CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
87	VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
88	VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
89	VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
90	                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
91	                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
92	
93	.PHONY: all clean dump rv32
94	
95	# Linux-ABI app fixtures (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U3+): -nostdlib, no
96	# andesim runtime at all -- vlinux is what sets these up, not crt0.S. Link
97	# base 0x10000, the roadmap's "App image" base; -e _start since there is no
98	# crt0 to fall into it via link order.
99	LINUX_APP_CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
100	LINUX_APP_LDFLAGS := -nostdlib -static -Wl,-e,_start -Wl,-Ttext=0x10000
101	
102	# Real static-glibc app fixtures (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4+): the vendor
103	# Linux-ABI toolchain (separate from HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN's bare-metal newlib
104	# one), ordinary static link -- no -Ttext override, the toolchain's own
105	# default static-exec layout (non-PIE, link base ~0x50000) just works with
106	# vlinux's loader as-is. Deferred to use-time (recursive `=` + $(error)) so
107	# `make all` (which does not need LINUX_TOOLCHAIN) is unaffected.
108	linux_glibc_tc = $(if $(strip $(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)),$(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN),$(error LINUX_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass LINUX_TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
109	GLIBC_CC = $(linux_glibc_tc)/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc
110	
111	all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
112	     rt_linux_argv.elf \
113	     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
114	     hvm_readback.elf \
115	     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
116	     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
117	     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)
118	
119	# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
120	# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
121	# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.
122	
123	spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
124		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
125		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@
126	
127	handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
128		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
129		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@
130	
131	rt_linux_argv.elf: rt_linux_argv.c
132		$(CC) $(LINUX_APP_CFLAGS) $(LINUX_APP_LDFLAGS) $< -o $@
133	
134	# Static-glibc app fixtures sharing one toolchain/link (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md):
135	#   rt_linux_glibc_hello  U4: hello world
136	#   rt_linux_file         U5: file I/O syscall set
137	#   rt_linux_time         U6: time syscalls
138	#   rt_linux_mmap         U7: file-backed private mmap
139	# NOT part of `all` -- they need the optional LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (env-gated, like
140	# the rv32 fixtures need HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32). Build individually:
141	# make rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf
142	RT_LINUX_GLIBC_FIXTURES := rt_linux_glibc_hello rt_linux_file rt_linux_time \
143	                           rt_linux_mmap
144	$(RT_LINUX_GLIBC_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c
145		$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall $< -o $@
146	
147	# ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U9: marker'd glibc kernel under hybrid. Same
148	# toolchain/link, plus the installed andesim/ROI.h include path (the same
149	# runtime/ build every vplat fixture uses via -B/-specs -- this fixture
150	# just needs the ONE header, not the whole bare-metal runtime).
151	rt_linux_matvec.elf: rt_linux_matvec.c $(VPLAT_RT)
152		$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall \
153		  -I $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include $< -o $@
154	
155	# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
156	# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
157	# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
158	# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
159	l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
160		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
161		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
162	lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
163	
164	# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content through the hart-local
165	# TCM view AND the slave-port aperture on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for
166	# the exit code).
167	lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h \
168	                 $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
169		$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
170	
171	# HVM transport (F1, ROADMAP_hvm): reads back --hvm content through the
172	# 0x90000000 subordinate-port aperture on the cycle engine.
173	hvm_readback.elf: hvm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
174		$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
175	
176	$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
177		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
178		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
179	
180	# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
181	# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
182	$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
183		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
184		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
185	
186	# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
187	# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
188	$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
189		$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
190		  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
191	
192	# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
193	# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
194	$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
195		$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
196		  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
197	rt_c_hvm_data.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
198	
199	# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
200	# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
201	$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
202		$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
203	
204	# C++ smoke fixture: the g++ driver adds -lstdc++ -lm itself; everything
205	# else (crt0, crtbegin/crtend, andesim.ld, lib group) comes from the specs.
206	$(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.cpp $(VPLAT_RT)
207		$(CXX) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
208	
209	# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
210	$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
211		$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)
212	
213	# Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
214	# pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
215	# source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
216	# (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
217	# same GEMM kernel.
218	rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
219		$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
220		  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@
221	
222	# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
223	rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf
224	
225	rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
226		$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
227		$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@
228	
229	rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
230		$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
231		  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@
232	
233	# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
234	$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
235		$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)
236	
237	dump: spin.elf
238		$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
239	
240	clean:
241		rm -f spin.o spin.elf \
242		      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
243		      rt_linux_argv.elf $(RT_LINUX_GLIBC_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
244		      rt_linux_matvec.elf \
245		      l2c_drain.o l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.o wm_drain.elf \
246		      lm_drain.o lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf hvm_readback.elf \
247		      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
248		      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
249		      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
250		      $(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
251		      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
252		      rv32_spin.o rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
CXX       = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-g++
LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill \
                    rt_c_hvm_data
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file vplat_gettimeofday \
                       vplat_window
# C++ vplat smoke fixture: static ctors/dtors + libstdc++ containers
# through the same two-flag link, with g++ instead of gcc.
RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_cpp

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/htif_client.c $(RUNTIME_DIR)/htif_client.h \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

# Linux-ABI app fixtures (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U3+): -nostdlib, no
# andesim runtime at all -- vlinux is what sets these up, not crt0.S. Link
# base 0x10000, the roadmap's "App image" base; -e _start since there is no
# crt0 to fall into it via link order.
LINUX_APP_CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LINUX_APP_LDFLAGS := -nostdlib -static -Wl,-e,_start -Wl,-Ttext=0x10000

# Real static-glibc app fixtures (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4+): the vendor
# Linux-ABI toolchain (separate from HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN's bare-metal newlib
# one), ordinary static link -- no -Ttext override, the toolchain's own
# default static-exec layout (non-PIE, link base ~0x50000) just works with
# vlinux's loader as-is. Deferred to use-time (recursive `=` + $(error)) so
# `make all` (which does not need LINUX_TOOLCHAIN) is unaffected.
linux_glibc_tc = $(if $(strip $(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)),$(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN),$(error LINUX_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass LINUX_TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
GLIBC_CC = $(linux_glibc_tc)/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc

all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     rt_linux_argv.elf \
     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
     hvm_readback.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

rt_linux_argv.elf: rt_linux_argv.c
	$(CC) $(LINUX_APP_CFLAGS) $(LINUX_APP_LDFLAGS) $< -o $@

# Static-glibc app fixtures sharing one toolchain/link (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md):
#   rt_linux_glibc_hello  U4: hello world
#   rt_linux_file         U5: file I/O syscall set
#   rt_linux_time         U6: time syscalls
#   rt_linux_mmap         U7: file-backed private mmap
# NOT part of `all` -- they need the optional LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (env-gated, like
# the rv32 fixtures need HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32). Build individually:
# make rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf
RT_LINUX_GLIBC_FIXTURES := rt_linux_glibc_hello rt_linux_file rt_linux_time \
                           rt_linux_mmap
$(RT_LINUX_GLIBC_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c
	$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall $< -o $@

# ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U9: marker'd glibc kernel under hybrid. Same
# toolchain/link, plus the installed andesim/ROI.h include path (the same
# runtime/ build every vplat fixture uses via -B/-specs -- this fixture
# just needs the ONE header, not the whole bare-metal runtime).
rt_linux_matvec.elf: rt_linux_matvec.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall \
	  -I $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include $< -o $@

# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content through the hart-local
# TCM view AND the slave-port aperture on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for
# the exit code).
lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h \
                 $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# HVM transport (F1, ROADMAP_hvm): reads back --hvm content through the
# 0x90000000 subordinate-port aperture on the cycle engine.
hvm_readback.elf: hvm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
rt_c_hvm_data.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# C++ smoke fixture: the g++ driver adds -lstdc++ -lm itself; everything
# else (crt0, crtbegin/crtend, andesim.ld, lib group) comes from the specs.
$(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.cpp $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CXX) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
# pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
# source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
# (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
# same GEMM kernel.
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

dump: spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      rt_linux_argv.elf $(RT_LINUX_GLIBC_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_linux_matvec.elf \
	      l2c_drain.o l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.o wm_drain.elf \
	      lm_drain.o lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf hvm_readback.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rv32_spin.o rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

# vlinux: M-mode proxy-kernel skeleton (U1, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md).
#
# Reuses ../../build/runtime/crt0.o and libandesim_runtime.a VERBATIM:
# crt0.S's cache/FS/VS/UNA bring-up and the HTIF UART/exit stubs use only
# PC-relative addressing and a linker-provided _stack symbol, so the same
# object already works at vlinux's load address (0x0200_0000) with no
# vlinux-specific fork. main.c (banner + manifest), vlinux.ld (link base +
# .manifest section), loader.c (ELF read + PT_LOAD mapping), stack.c (Linux
# initial stack + auxv), mm.c (brk/mmap arenas) and syscall.c (the app's
# ecall dispatch, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U3/U4) are vlinux-specific.
#
# Output: ../../build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
TRIPLE    := riscv64-unknown-elf
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-gcc

ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh`, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path)
endif

CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

RUNTIME_DIR := ..
RT_DIR      := ../../build/runtime
OUT         := ../../build/runtime/linux
# The shared hybrid ABI header (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md
# U9's loader.c overlap check) -- C and C++ both compile it (see the header's
# own comment); already included the same way by qemu_plugin/Makefile.
HYBRID_INCLUDE := ../../include

.PHONY: all clean rtlib

all: $(OUT)/vlinux.elf

$(OUT):
	mkdir -p $@

# The shared runtime lib + crt0.o (make -C .. is a fast no-op when
# already up to date, so this always runs rather than duplicating
# runtime/'s own source-file dependency list here).
rtlib:
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

SRCS := main.c loader.c stack.c mm.c syscall.c
HDRS := manifest.h loader.h stack.h mm.h vlinux_mem.h linux_errno.h \
        ../ecall_hook.h ../htif_client.h \
        $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi.h

$(OUT)/vlinux.elf: $(SRCS) $(HDRS) vlinux.ld rtlib | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I $(HYBRID_INCLUDE) -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs \
	  -T vlinux.ld \
	  $(RT_DIR)/crt0.o $(SRCS) \
	  -L $(RT_DIR) -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group \
	  -o $@

clean:
	rm -rf $(OUT)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# andesim: repo-root entry for the C++ driver (build/andesim).
# Self-bootstraps on first use so a fresh clone can run ./andesim
# directly; the build is host-only (no Verilator/SystemC/QEMU needed).
#
# macOS is run-only: both legs must share one Linux kernel, so the wrapper
# re-execs inside the prebuilt runtime image (podman machine VM); the shared
# mmap then lives in the VM, never on a virtiofs mount. ANDESIM_OS is a
# test hook to force the branch from Linux.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

if [ "${ANDESIM_OS:-$(uname -s)}" = "Darwin" ]; then
  exec bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_in_container.sh" "$@"
fi

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >&2
exec "$BIN" "$@"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
3	# replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
4	#
5	# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
6	#   lint      tests/test_*.sh + roi.test.sh + the fixture ROI-content lint
7	#             (fast harness self-checks; no engine spawns. The one heavy
8	#             harness test, tests/test_kernel_cycles.sh, stays manual: it
9	#             runs real QEMU+vsim round-trips the e2e phase already covers.)
10	#   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
11	#   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
12	#   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
13	#
14	# Usage:
15	#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [lint|unit|contract|e2e ...]
16	#
17	# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
18	# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
19	# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
20	set -uo pipefail
21	
22	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
23	
24	DRY_RUN=0
25	PHASES=()
26	for arg in "$@"; do
27	  case "$arg" in
28	    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
29	    lint|unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
30	    *)
31	      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
32	      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [lint|unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
33	      exit 2
34	      ;;
35	  esac
36	done
37	[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(lint unit contract e2e)
38	
39	step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
40	ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
41	fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
42	
43	pass=0
44	failed=0
45	declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
46	
47	# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
48	run_case() {
49	  local name="$1"; shift
50	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
51	  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
52	  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
53	  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
54	    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
55	  else
56	    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
57	    cat "$log"
58	  fi
59	  rm -f "$log"
60	}
61	
62	run_lint() {
63	  step "[lint] harness self-checks"
64	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
65	    printf '  %s\n' "tests/test_*.sh (each; kernel_cycles excluded)" \
66	      "tests/lib/roi.test.sh" "tests/fixtures/test_fixture_roi_content.sh"
67	    return
68	  fi
69	  local s
70	  for s in "$ROOT"/tests/test_*.sh; do
71	    [ -f "$s" ] || continue
72	    # Heavy manual smoke test (real QEMU+vsim runs); e2e covers the surface.
73	    [ "$(basename "$s")" = "test_kernel_cycles.sh" ] && continue
74	    run_case "[lint] $(basename "$s")" bash "$s"
75	  done
76	  run_case "[lint] roi.test.sh" bash "$ROOT/tests/lib/roi.test.sh"
77	  run_case "[lint] test_fixture_roi_content.sh" \
78	    bash "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/test_fixture_roi_content.sh"
79	}
80	
81	run_unit() {
82	  step "[unit] C++ driver unit tests"
83	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
84	    printf '  %s\n' "scripts/build_driver.sh" "build/driver/andesim-*-test (each)"
85	    return
86	  fi
87	  if ! bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null; then
88	    fail "[unit] build_driver.sh failed"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
89	  fi
90	  shopt -s nullglob
91	  local bins=("$ROOT"/build/driver/andesim-*-test)
92	  shopt -u nullglob
93	  if [ "${#bins[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
94	    fail "[unit] no unit-test binaries under build/driver"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
95	  fi
96	  local t
97	  for t in "${bins[@]}"; do run_case "[unit] $(basename "$t")" "$t"; done
98	}
99

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
#
# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
#   lint      tests/test_*.sh + roi.test.sh + the fixture ROI-content lint
#             (fast harness self-checks; no engine spawns. The one heavy
#             harness test, tests/test_kernel_cycles.sh, stays manual: it
#             runs real QEMU+vsim round-trips the e2e phase already covers.)
#   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
#   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
#   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [lint|unit|contract|e2e ...]
#
# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

DRY_RUN=0
PHASES=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    lint|unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
    *)
      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [lint|unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done
[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(lint unit contract e2e)

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

pass=0
failed=0
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()

# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
run_case() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
  else
    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
    cat "$log"
  fi
  rm -f "$log"
}

run_lint() {
  step "[lint] harness self-checks"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "tests/test_*.sh (each; kernel_cycles excluded)" \
      "tests/lib/roi.test.sh" "tests/fixtures/test_fixture_roi_content.sh"
    return
  fi
  local s
  for s in "$ROOT"/tests/test_*.sh; do
    [ -f "$s" ] || continue
    # Heavy manual smoke test (real QEMU+vsim runs); e2e covers the surface.
    [ "$(basename "$s")" = "test_kernel_cycles.sh" ] && continue
    run_case "[lint] $(basename "$s")" bash "$s"
  done
  run_case "[lint] roi.test.sh" bash "$ROOT/tests/lib/roi.test.sh"
  run_case "[lint] test_fixture_roi_content.sh" \
    bash "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/test_fixture_roi_content.sh"
}

run_unit() {
  step "[unit] C++ driver unit tests"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "scripts/build_driver.sh" "build/driver/andesim-*-test (each)"
    return
  fi
  if ! bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null; then
    fail "[unit] build_driver.sh failed"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
  fi
  shopt -s nullglob
  local bins=("$ROOT"/build/driver/andesim-*-test)
  shopt -u nullglob
  if [ "${#bins[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    fail "[unit] no unit-test binaries under build/driver"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
  fi
  local t
  for t in "${bins[@]}"; do run_case "[unit] $(basename "$t")" "$t"; done
}

run_contract() {
  step "[contract] driver feature + parity contracts"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh (each)" \
      "tests/andes_csr/test_*.sh (each)"
    return
  fi
  local s
  for s in "$ROOT"/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh \
           "$ROOT"/tests/andes_csr/test_*.sh; do
    [ -f "$s" ] || continue
    run_case "[contract] $(basename "$s")" bash "$s"
  done
}

run_e2e() {
  step "[e2e] hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "scripts/run_e2e.sh"; return; fi
  run_case "[e2e] run_e2e.sh" bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh"
}

for p in "${PHASES[@]}"; do
  case "$p" in
    lint)     run_lint ;;
    unit)     run_unit ;;
    contract) run_contract ;;
    e2e)      run_e2e ;;
  esac
done

if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
  echo
  echo "(dry-run: nothing executed)"
  exit 0
fi

echo
step "summary: $pass passed, $failed failed"
if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
  fail "failed: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Run the hybrid e2e tests. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts
3	# (source ./setup.sh first to export the external qemu/vsim locations).
4	#
5	# Env overrides:
6	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64)
7	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
8	#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: $VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_ax45mpv_premium,
9	#                falling back to the first sim_* only when the canonical
10	#                engine is not built -- see the comment at the default)
11	#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
12	#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
13	#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
14	#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
15	#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
16	#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
17	#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
18	#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
19	#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
20	#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
21	#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)
22	
23	set -euo pipefail
24	
25	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
26	
27	# Fill env gaps from ./config.env (the per-host file setup.sh maintains) so
28	# `scripts/test_all.sh e2e` works from a fresh shell. An exported value wins;
29	# the file only supplies what the caller's shell lacks -- same pattern as
30	# tests/lib. Exported for the child builds (make -C tests/fixtures).
31	cfg_val() { sed -n "s/^$1=//p" "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tail -1; }
32	for _k in QEMU_BIN_DIR VSIM_BIN_DIR HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 \
33	          LINUX_TOOLCHAIN; do
34	  if [[ -z "${!_k:-}" ]]; then
35	    _v="$(cfg_val "$_k")"
36	    [[ -n "$_v" ]] && export "$_k=$_v"
37	  fi
38	done
39	unset _k _v
40	
41	# vsim sim_* live in the external VSIM_BIN_DIR (setup.sh exports it, mirroring
42	# VSIM_QEMU); empty when neither setup.sh nor config.env supplied it -- the
43	# require below reports it.
44	VSIM_BUILD="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}"
45	HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
46	TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"
47	
48	VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
49	VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
50	if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
51	  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
52	  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
53	  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under $VSIM_BIN_DIR -- the
54	  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
55	  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
56	  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
57	  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
58	  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
59	    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_BUILD"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
60	  fi
61	fi
62	
63	step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
64	ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
65	warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
66	fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
67	
68	require() {
69	  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
70	    fail "$1 not found: $2"
71	    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
72	    exit 1
73	  fi
74	}
75	require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
76	require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
77	require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"
78	
79	export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN
80	
81	# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
82	# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
83	# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
84	# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
85	RT_TESTS=(
86	  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
87	  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
88	  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
89	  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
90	  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
91	  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
92	  "rt_all_fprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_fprs"
93	  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
94	  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
95	  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
96	  "rt_m_ext_counters|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_counters"
97	  "rt_m_ext_trigcause|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_trigcause"
98	  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
99	  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
100	  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
101	  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
102	  "rt_c_fcsr|FIXTURE=rt_c_fcsr"
103	  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
104	  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
105	  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
106	  "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
107	  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
108	  "rt_c_dlm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_dlm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=DLM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
109	  "rt_c_ilm_code|FIXTURE=rt_c_ilm_code CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=ILM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1"
110	  "rt_c_hvm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_hvm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=HVM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
111	)
112	
113	NEG_TESTS=(
114	  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
115	  "rt_lm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_lm_transport_off.sh"
116	  "rt_hvm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_hvm_transport_off.sh"
117	)
118	
119	# Heavyweight round-trip fixtures, run SEQUENTIALLY after the parallel
120	# pool drains. The L6 privilege fixtures need an S/U-capable engine pair
121	# (the default ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only,
122	# NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1), and the only built RV64 one is
123	# ax66_makatau -- whose Verilator binary runs 32 threads. Two of those in
124	# the parallel pool saturate the box and time out BOTH themselves and the
125	# lighter default-engine tests, so they get the machine to themselves.
126	# Same entry format as RT_TESTS; both trigger modes still apply.
127	SERIAL_RT_TESTS=(
128	  "rt_priv_smode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_smode CHECK_PRIV=1 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
129	  "rt_priv_umode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_umode CHECK_PRIV=0 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
130	)
131	
132	# Fixture auto-build gate: the required ELF set is DERIVED from the test
133	# tables above (each entry's FIXTURE= token), so it cannot drift from the
134	# tests that consume the ELFs. The NEG_TESTS drivers reuse fixtures
135	# already named in RT_TESTS (handoff_roundtrip, rt_c_dlm_data,
136	# rt_c_hvm_data), so no separate list is needed for them.
137	need_build=0
138	for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}" "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
139	  fixture=""
140	  for tok in ${entry#*|}; do
141	    case "$tok" in FIXTURE=*) fixture="${tok#FIXTURE=}" ;; esac
142	  done
143	  if [[ -n "$fixture" && ! -e "$TEST_DIR/$fixture.elf" ]]; then
144	    need_build=1
145	  fi
146	done
147	if (( need_build )); then
148	  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
149	  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
150	fi
151	
152	MODE="${MODE:-both}"
153	case "$MODE" in
154	  marker|pc|both) ;;
155	  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
156	esac
157	
158	default_jobs() {
159	  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
160	  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
161	  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
162	    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
163	    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
164	      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
165	      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
166	    fi
167	  fi
168	  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
169	  printf '%d\n' "$n"
170	}
171	JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
172	[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
173	  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }
174	
175	FILTER="${FILTER:-}"
176	
177	LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
178	mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
179	RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
180	LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
181	: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
182	: > "$LOCK_FILE"
183	
184	# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
185	# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
186	# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
187	# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
188	# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
189	# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
190	# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
191	run_one() {
192	  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
193	  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
194	  local start end elapsed status rc
195	  start=$(date +%s)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the hybrid e2e tests. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts
# (source ./setup.sh first to export the external qemu/vsim locations).
#
# Env overrides:
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64)
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: $VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_ax45mpv_premium,
#                falling back to the first sim_* only when the canonical
#                engine is not built -- see the comment at the default)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# Fill env gaps from ./config.env (the per-host file setup.sh maintains) so
# `scripts/test_all.sh e2e` works from a fresh shell. An exported value wins;
# the file only supplies what the caller's shell lacks -- same pattern as
# tests/lib. Exported for the child builds (make -C tests/fixtures).
cfg_val() { sed -n "s/^$1=//p" "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tail -1; }
for _k in QEMU_BIN_DIR VSIM_BIN_DIR HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 \
          LINUX_TOOLCHAIN; do
  if [[ -z "${!_k:-}" ]]; then
    _v="$(cfg_val "$_k")"
    [[ -n "$_v" ]] && export "$_k=$_v"
  fi
done
unset _k _v

# vsim sim_* live in the external VSIM_BIN_DIR (setup.sh exports it, mirroring
# VSIM_QEMU); empty when neither setup.sh nor config.env supplied it -- the
# require below reports it.
VSIM_BUILD="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under $VSIM_BIN_DIR -- the
  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_BUILD"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
    exit 1
  fi
}
require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
RT_TESTS=(
  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
  "rt_all_fprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_fprs"
  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
  "rt_m_ext_counters|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_counters"
  "rt_m_ext_trigcause|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_trigcause"
  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_fcsr|FIXTURE=rt_c_fcsr"
  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
  "rt_c_dlm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_dlm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=DLM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_ilm_code|FIXTURE=rt_c_ilm_code CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=ILM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1"
  "rt_c_hvm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_hvm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=HVM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
)

NEG_TESTS=(
  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
  "rt_lm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_lm_transport_off.sh"
  "rt_hvm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_hvm_transport_off.sh"
)

# Heavyweight round-trip fixtures, run SEQUENTIALLY after the parallel
# pool drains. The L6 privilege fixtures need an S/U-capable engine pair
# (the default ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only,
# NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1), and the only built RV64 one is
# ax66_makatau -- whose Verilator binary runs 32 threads. Two of those in
# the parallel pool saturate the box and time out BOTH themselves and the
# lighter default-engine tests, so they get the machine to themselves.
# Same entry format as RT_TESTS; both trigger modes still apply.
SERIAL_RT_TESTS=(
  "rt_priv_smode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_smode CHECK_PRIV=1 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
  "rt_priv_umode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_umode CHECK_PRIV=0 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
)

# Fixture auto-build gate: the required ELF set is DERIVED from the test
# tables above (each entry's FIXTURE= token), so it cannot drift from the
# tests that consume the ELFs. The NEG_TESTS drivers reuse fixtures
# already named in RT_TESTS (handoff_roundtrip, rt_c_dlm_data,
# rt_c_hvm_data), so no separate list is needed for them.
need_build=0
for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}" "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
  fixture=""
  for tok in ${entry#*|}; do
    case "$tok" in FIXTURE=*) fixture="${tok#FIXTURE=}" ;; esac
  done
  if [[ -n "$fixture" && ! -e "$TEST_DIR/$fixture.elf" ]]; then
    need_build=1
  fi
done
if (( need_build )); then
  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
fi

MODE="${MODE:-both}"
case "$MODE" in
  marker|pc|both) ;;
  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
esac

default_jobs() {
  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
    fi
  fi
  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
  printf '%d\n' "$n"
}
JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }

FILTER="${FILTER:-}"

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
: > "$LOCK_FILE"

# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
run_one() {
  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
  local start end elapsed status rc
  start=$(date +%s)
  set +e
  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  set -e
  end=$(date +%s)
  elapsed=$((end - start))
  case $rc in
    0)  status=PASS ;;
    77) status=SKIP ;;
    *)  status=FAIL ;;
  esac
  (
    flock 9
    case "$status" in
      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
    esac
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
}

# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
declare -a WORKPLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done
for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
done

# Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
# after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done

TOTAL=$(( ${#WORKPLAN[@]} + ${#SERIAL_PLAN[@]} ))
step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"

# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
  printf '.\n' >&8
done

i=0
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  read -r -u 8 _tok
  (
    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
    printf '.\n' >&8
  ) &
done
wait
exec 8>&-

# Serial phase: each heavyweight test gets the machine to itself.
for w in "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
done

declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
  case "$r_status" in
    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
  esac
done < "$RESULTS_FILE"

# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
# deterministic post-run failure dump.
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}" "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
    echo
    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
  fi
done

echo
marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
total_pass=$((marker_p + pc_p + neg_p))
total_fail=$((marker_f + pc_f + neg_f))
total_skip=$((marker_s + pc_s + neg_s))
step "summary: marker ${marker_p}p/${marker_f}f/${marker_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

input.command:
echo "=== TEST COUNTS ===" 
printf 'tests/test_*.sh (lint):      %s\n' "$(ls tests/test_*.sh 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"

printf 'unit bins in build/driver:   %s\n' "$(ls build/driver/andesim-*-test 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"
ls build/driver/andesim-*-test 2>/dev/null
printf 'tests/andes_sim/*.sh:        %s\n' "$(ls tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh | wc -l)"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Driver: build the plugin (qemu and vsim are external, prebuilt), then add the
3	# external build dirs to PATH.
4	# Source this script to affect your current shell's PATH:
5	#   source ./setup.sh                       # build all
6	#   source ./setup.sh clean [target]        # clean vsim|plugin|all (default: all)
7	
8	if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
9	  _SETUP_SRC="${(%):-%x}"
10	elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
11	  _SETUP_SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
12	else
13	  _SETUP_SRC="$0"
14	fi
15	
16	# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
17	# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
18	# under nounset).
19	_hybrid_setup_main() {
20	  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
21	    emulate -L sh
22	    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
23	  else
24	    local -
25	    set -euo pipefail
26	  fi
27	
28	  # QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR are NOT in this local list: they are exported
29	  # for the caller's shell at the end of this function, and exporting a local
30	  # dies at function return (the shell pops the scope, children never see it).
31	  local ROOT PLUGIN_DIR PLUGIN_SO CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE _arch
32	  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
33	  # QEMU_BIN_DIR and VSIM_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* and vsim
34	  # sim_* build directories) both come from config.env -- this project integrates
35	  # a prebuilt QEMU and a prebuilt external vsim; it builds neither.
36	  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
37	  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
38	  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
39	  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"
40	
41	  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
42	  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
43	  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
44	
45	  clean_vsim()   { step "vsim is external (${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-unset})"; ok "not cleaned here -- clean it in your external vsim checkout"; }
46	  clean_plugin() {
47	    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
48	    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
49	      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
50	    else
51	      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
52	    fi
53	    ok "plugin cleaned"
54	  }
55	
56	  if [ "${1:-}" = "clean" ]; then
57	    case "${2:-all}" in
58	      vsim)     clean_vsim ;;
59	      plugin)   clean_plugin ;;
60	      all)      clean_vsim; clean_plugin ;;
61	      *)        err "usage: source $_SETUP_SRC clean [vsim|plugin|all]"; return 1 ;;
62	    esac
63	    return 0
64	  fi
65	
66	  step "0/3 loading per-host config"
67	  if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
68	    if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]; then
69	      err "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE"
70	      return 1
71	    fi
72	    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
73	    ok "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchain lives elsewhere"
74	  fi
75	  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
76	  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
77	  if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]; then
78	    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set; check $CONFIG_FILE"
79	    return 1
80	  fi
81	  if [ ! -d "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin" ]; then
82	    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN has no bin/ directory; edit $CONFIG_FILE"
83	    return 1
84	  fi
85	  export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
86	  ok "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"
87	
88	  step "1/3 locating external qemu (rv32 + rv64)"
89	  if [ -z "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
90	    err "QEMU_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your qemu-system-* build dir in $CONFIG_FILE"
91	    return 1
92	  fi
93	  for _arch in riscv32 riscv64; do
94	    if [ ! -x "$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-$_arch" ]; then
95	      err "no qemu-system-$_arch under QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR; build both rv32+rv64 QEMU there or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
96	      return 1
97	    fi
98	  done
99	  ok "qemu <- $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-{riscv32,riscv64} (external, prebuilt)"
100	
101	  step "2/3 locating external vsim"
102	  if [ -z "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
103	    err "VSIM_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your external vsim build dir (holding sim_* binaries) in $CONFIG_FILE"
104	    return 1
105	  fi
106	  if ! ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
107	    err "no sim_* under VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR; build vsim in your external checkout or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
108	    return 1
109	  fi
110	  ok "vsim <- $VSIM_BIN_DIR (external, prebuilt)"
111	
112	  step "3/3 building hybrid plugin"
113	  if [ ! -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
114	    err "missing $PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile"
115	    return 1
116	  fi
117	  # Plugins build against the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h -- no
118	  # QEMU source tree required.
119	  make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR"
120	  ok "plugin -> $PLUGIN_SO"
121	
122	  step "PATH: prepending build dirs"
123	  case ":$PATH:" in
124	    *":$QEMU_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
125	    *) export PATH="$QEMU_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
126	  esac
127	  case ":$PATH:" in
128	    *":$VSIM_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
129	    *) export PATH="$VSIM_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
130	  esac
131	  ok "PATH updated (this shell only)"
132	
133	  step "env: exporting QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR / VSIM_QEMU{,32} / VSIM_PLUGIN for the driver + e2e scripts"
134	  export QEMU_BIN_DIR
135	  export VSIM_BIN_DIR
136	  export VSIM_QEMU="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64"
137	  export VSIM_QEMU32="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv32"
138	  export VSIM_PLUGIN="$PLUGIN_SO"
139	  ok "QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR"
140	  ok "VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR (external vsim; the driver discovers engines here)"
141	  ok "VSIM_QEMU=$VSIM_QEMU"
142	  ok "VSIM_QEMU32=$VSIM_QEMU32"
143	  ok "VSIM_PLUGIN=$VSIM_PLUGIN"
144	
145	  if [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ] && [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" = "${0:-}" ]; then
146	    err "script was executed, not sourced - PATH change is local to this subshell"
147	    err "to update your shell, run: source $_SETUP_SRC"
148	  fi
149	}
150	
151	_hybrid_setup_main "$@"
