#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Driver: build the plugin (qemu and vsim are external, prebuilt), then add the
# external build dirs to PATH.
# Source this script to affect your current shell's PATH:
#   source ./setup.sh                       # build all
#   source ./setup.sh clean [target]        # clean vsim|plugin|all (default: all)

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${(%):-%x}"
elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
else
  _SETUP_SRC="$0"
fi

# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
# under nounset).
_hybrid_setup_main() {
  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    emulate -L sh
    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
  else
    local -
    set -euo pipefail
  fi

  # QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR are NOT in this local list: they are exported
  # for the caller's shell at the end of this function, and exporting a local
  # dies at function return (the shell pops the scope, children never see it).
  local ROOT PLUGIN_DIR PLUGIN_SO CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE _arch
  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
  # QEMU_BIN_DIR and VSIM_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* and vsim
  # sim_* build directories) both come from config.env -- this project integrates
  # a prebuilt QEMU and a prebuilt external vsim; it builds neither.
  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

  clean_vsim()   { step "vsim is external (${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-unset})"; ok "not cleaned here -- clean it in your external vsim checkout"; }
  clean_plugin() {
    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
    else
      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
    fi
    ok "plugin cleaned"
  }

  if [ "${1:-}" = "clean" ]; then
    case "${2:-all}" in
      vsim)     clean_vsim ;;
      plugin)   clean_plugin ;;
      all)      clean_vsim; clean_plugin ;;
      *)        err "usage: source $_SETUP_SRC clean [vsim|plugin|all]"; return 1 ;;
    esac
    return 0
  fi

  step "0/3 loading per-host config"
  if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
    if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]; then
      err "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
    ok "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchain lives elsewhere"
  fi
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
  if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set; check $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ ! -d "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN has no bin/ directory; edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
  ok "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"

  step "1/3 locating external qemu (rv32 + rv64)"
  if [ -z "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "QEMU_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your qemu-system-* build dir in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  for _arch in riscv32 riscv64; do
    if [ ! -x "$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-$_arch" ]; then
      err "no qemu-system-$_arch under QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR; build both rv32+rv64 QEMU there or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
  done
  ok "qemu <- $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-{riscv32,riscv64} (external, prebuilt)"

  step "2/3 locating external vsim"
  if [ -z "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "VSIM_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your external vsim build dir (holding sim_* binaries) in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if ! ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "no sim_* under VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR; build vsim in your external checkout or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  ok "vsim <- $VSIM_BIN_DIR (external, prebuilt)"

  step "3/3 building hybrid plugin"
  if [ ! -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
    err "missing $PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile"
    return 1
  fi
  # Plugins build against the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h -- no
  # QEMU source tree required.
  make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR"
  ok "plugin -> $PLUGIN_SO"

  step "PATH: prepending build dirs"
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$QEMU_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$QEMU_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$VSIM_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$VSIM_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  ok "PATH updated (this shell only)"

  step "env: exporting QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR / VSIM_QEMU{,32} / VSIM_PLUGIN for the driver + e2e scripts"
  export QEMU_BIN_DIR
  export VSIM_BIN_DIR
  export VSIM_QEMU="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64"
  export VSIM_QEMU32="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv32"
  export VSIM_PLUGIN="$PLUGIN_SO"
  ok "QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR"
  ok "VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR (external vsim; the driver discovers engines here)"
  ok "VSIM_QEMU=$VSIM_QEMU"
  ok "VSIM_QEMU32=$VSIM_QEMU32"
  ok "VSIM_PLUGIN=$VSIM_PLUGIN"

  if [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ] && [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" = "${0:-}" ]; then
    err "script was executed, not sourced - PATH change is local to this subshell"
    err "to update your shell, run: source $_SETUP_SRC"
  fi
}

_hybrid_setup_main "$@"
unset -f _hybrid_setup_main 2>/dev/null
unset _SETUP_SRC

=== tests/lib/paths.sh ===
# Shared path resolution for the top-level e2e harness + drivers.
# Sourced (not executed). Provides:
#   TOP_ROOT                  - absolute path of the repo root
#   hybrid_resolve_paths()    - sets VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN,
#                               VSIM_ELF from TOP_ROOT (unless already
#                               exported by caller) and exits 77 (CTest
#                               skip) if any artifact is missing. Reads
#                               FIXTURE for the VSIM_ELF default.
#   hybrid_describe_int F [BIN] - print integer field F from an engine's
#                               --describe JSON (BIN defaults to $VSIM_BIN);
#                               empty output if absent/unprobeable. The ONE
#                               shell parser of the descriptor wire format.
#   plugin_qemu_drain LOG ARGS [QEMU_ARGS...] - spawn QEMU for a plugin-only
#                               drain test (boots $VSIM_ELF with the plugin
#                               attached); sets RC to QEMU's exit code.

TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)

if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then
  . "$TOP_ROOT/config.env"
fi

hybrid_resolve_paths() {
  # VSIM_BIN_DIR / QEMU_BIN_DIR come from the environment or from the
  # config.env sourced above; there is no in-tree fallback (both simulators
  # are external prebuilts). Unset -> a nonexistent path -> skip below.
  VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
  VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
  VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
  VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
  for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
    if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
      echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
      exit 77
    fi
  done
}

# Extract one integer field from an engine's --describe JSON. $1 = field name,
# $2 = engine binary (default $VSIM_BIN). Prints nothing when the field is
# absent or the binary cannot be probed, so callers can `[ -n ... ]`-gate.
hybrid_describe_int() {
  "${2:-$VSIM_BIN}" --describe 2>/dev/null \
    | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" | head -n1
}

# Code Coverage Feasibility Report — `/home/nick/work/andesim`

## 0. Headline

- **There is NO `src/` directory.** The C++ `andesim` driver lives in **`/home/nick/work/andesim/driver/`** (21 `.cpp` + headers, ~10.6k lines).
- **There is ZERO existing code-coverage infrastructure.** Every `coverage` hit in the repo is a *domain* term (CSR transport coverage matrices), not gcov/lcov.
- **Host-coverage-able:** `driver/*.cpp` (C++20, CMake) and `qemu_plugin/*.c` (host C, `.so` loaded into QEMU). **Not coverage-able the normal way:** `runtime/`, `runtime/linux/`, `tests/fixtures/` — all cross-compiled bare-metal RISC-V.
- **Host toolchain is ready:** gcc/gcov 16.1.1 and clang/llvm-cov/llvm-profdata 22.1.6 are installed. **`lcov`, `genhtml`, `gcovr`, `kcov` are NOT installed.**

---

## 1. Build system — what builds what

### 1.1 Orchestrator: `/home/nick/work/andesim/scripts/build_all.sh`

Only orchestrates; contains no compiler invocations (lines 58-64):

```bash
case "$TARGET" in
  all)      run bash "$ROOT/setup.sh"; run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures"; run make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" ;;
  plugin)   run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_qemu_plugin.sh" ;;
  fixtures) run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
  runtime)  run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_runtime.sh" ;;
  vlinux)   run make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" ;;
esac
```

Critically (lines 25-26):
```
# The andesim driver itself is NOT built here: ./andesim self-bootstraps via
# scripts/build_driver.sh on first use.
```

### 1.2 `/home/nick/work/andesim/setup.sh` (must be **sourced**)

Loads `config.env` (copying from `config.env.example` on first run), validates `QEMU_BIN_DIR` + `VSIM_BIN_DIR`, then the only build it does is the plugin (line 119): `make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR"`. Exports `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`, `QEMU_BIN_DIR`, `VSIM_BIN_DIR`, `VSIM_QEMU`, `VSIM_QEMU32`, `VSIM_PLUGIN`.

### 1.3 `/home/nick/work/andesim/config.env.example`

Plain `KEY=value` lines, no flags. Keys: `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`, `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32`, `LINUX_TOOLCHAIN`, `LLAMA_CPP_DIR`, `QEMU_BIN_DIR`, `VSIM_BIN_DIR`. `config.env` is gitignored. **No CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS hook exists here** — that would be a natural place to add a coverage toggle, but nothing reads such a key today.

### 1.4 HOST C++ driver — `/home/nick/work/andesim/driver/CMakeLists.txt`

```cmake
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(andes_sim CXX)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)
if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()
...
target_compile_options(andesim PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)
```
and for every test target (lines 81-84):
```cmake
foreach(_t andesim-cli-test ... andesim-vlinux-mem-test)
  target_compile_options(${_t} PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)
  set_target_properties(${_t} PROPERTIES RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR})
endforeach()
```

**Override-ability: GOOD.** No `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS` is set in the CMakeLists, so the standard CMake channels work:
- `CXXFLAGS=... cmake -S driver -B build/driver` (env, honored only on **first** configure), or
- `cmake ... -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="--coverage" -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="--coverage"` (cached, persists across rebuilds).

Current cache state (`/home/nick/work/andesim/build/driver/CMakeCache.txt`):
```
CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE:STRING=Release
CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER:FILEPATH=/usr/bin/c++
CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS:STRING=
CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE:STRING=-O3 -DNDEBUG
CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS:STRING=
CMAKE_GENERATOR:INTERNAL=Unix Makefiles
```
Note `-O3 -DNDEBUG` from Release — for meaningful line coverage you want `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug` or add `-O0 -g`.

### 1.5 Driver self-build — `/home/nick/work/andesim/scripts/build_driver.sh` (the "self-builds on first use" mechanism)

The **exact** code, lines 15-20:
```bash
cmake -S "$ROOT/driver" -B "$BUILD" \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY="$ROOT/build" \
  >/dev/null

cmake --build "$BUILD" -j"$(nproc)"
```

Triggered by `/home/nick/work/andesim/andesim` (19-line bash wrapper), lines 17-19:
```bash
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >&2
exec "$BIN" "$@"
```

**Coverage-relevant behavior:** `build_driver.sh` re-runs `cmake` on **every** invocation with only those two `-D` flags. Because CMake caches, a one-time `cmake -B build/driver -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="--coverage" ...` **survives** subsequent `build_driver.sh` calls (it does not reset `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS`). But it also **pins `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`** on every call, so you cannot get Debug to stick via the cache — put `-O0 -g` inside `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS` instead.

Callers of `build_driver.sh` (all will silently rebuild mid-run and reuse your instrumented cache):
- `/home/nick/work/andesim/andesim:18`
- `/home/nick/work/andesim/scripts/test_all.sh:87`
- `/home/nick/work/andesim/tests/lib/log.sh:55` (`build_driver()`, used by `require_driver()` in ~every contract test)
- `/home/nick/work/andesim/tests/plugin/test_plugin_hotIterationLoop_measure.sh:35`
- `/home/nick/work/andesim/Dockerfile.runtime:36`

Nothing anywhere does `rm -rf build/driver` (only `tests/vplat/test_vplat_f9.sh:20` does `rm -rf "$ROOT/build/runtime"` — the RISC-V runtime, unrelated).

### 1.6 HOST C plugin — `/home/nick/work/andesim/qemu_plugin/Makefile`

```make
CC ?= gcc

GLIB_CFLAGS := $(shell pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0)
GLIB_LIBS   := $(shell pkg-config --libs   glib-2.0)

CFLAGS  := -O2 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -std=c11
HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include
QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE := include
INCLUDES := -I$(HYBRID_INCLUDE) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS)
LDFLAGS := -shared
LIBS    := $(GLIB_LIBS)
```
Recipes:
```make
libhybrid_handoff.so: hybrid_handoff.c ...
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hybrid_handoff.c $(LIBS)

libhotIterationLoop.so: hotIterationLoop.c $(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE)/qemu-plugin.h
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hotIterationLoop.c $(LIBS)
```

**Override-ability: POOR.** `CFLAGS :=` is a simple (recursively-immediate) assignment, so the **environment `CFLAGS` is ignored**. Only `CC` and `HYBRID_INCLUDE` use `?=`. There is **no `+=` and no `override` anywhere** in any Makefile in this repo. The only way in is `make -C qemu_plugin CFLAGS='-O2 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -std=c11 --coverage'` on the command line — which **replaces the whole variable**, so you must re-state `-fPIC` or the shared-object link breaks. ### 2.3 Plugin-coverage gotcha

`libhybrid_handoff.so` is `dlopen`ed by QEMU. `.gcda` files are flushed by the `gcov` atexit handler, which runs on normal process exit. QEMU normally exits cleanly, so this works, **but**:
- `tests/e2e.sh:193` wraps QEMU in `timeout "$TIMEOUT"` → SIGTERM kill = **no `.gcda` written** for timed-out runs.
- `.gcda` paths are baked as absolute paths to `/home/nick/work/andesim/qemu_plugin/` at compile time; use `GCOV_PREFIX`/`GCOV_PREFIX_STRIP` to redirect for parallel runs, since `scripts/run_e2e.sh` runs up to `JOBS` QEMUs concurrently and concurrent `.gcda` merges are racy.

### 2.4 Driver-coverage gotcha (`fork`/`exec`)

The driver forks and execs the two simulator legs:
- `/home/nick/work/andesim/driver/process.cpp:30-31` — `execvp(cargv[0], cargv.data()); _exit(127);`
- `/home/nick/work/andesim/driver/cmd_profile.cpp:112-113` — same pattern
- forks at `driver/process.cpp:52,77,206` and `driver/cmd_profile.cpp:93`

`_exit()` **skips the gcov atexit flush**, and the forked child inherits a copy of the parent's counters — so on the exec-failure path (`_exit(127)`) you lose data, and on the normal path `execvp` replaces the image (counters discarded, which is correct — the parent still flushes its own). Net: parent-process coverage is fine; no double-counting. This is benign but worth knowing.

Also `/home/nick/work/andesim/andesim:19` does `exec "$BIN" "$@"` — a plain bash exec, harmless.
